whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Dealing with Insurance

items.title: California's Two-Year Clock
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury lawsuit in California, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity was involved. An attorney can help you figure out which deadline applies before it's too late.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Work Against You
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning your compensation can be reduced by any percentage of blame assigned to you — even if you're only slightly at fault. Insurers often use recorded statements to shift blame your way, so it's worth speaking with an attorney before giving one.

items.title: No Cap on Non-Economic Damages
items.desc: Unlike some states, California doesn't limit compensation for pain, suffering, and other non-economic losses in most car accident cases. An attorney can help make sure those losses are properly documented and valued, not just your medical bills.

items.question: I was in a crash on Rt 97 near Dorris — what should I do first?
items.answer: Get medical attention even if you feel okay, since some injuries show up later. Try to document the scene, get contact info for any witnesses, and avoid giving a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer until you've talked to an attorney. LawProactive can connect you with someone familiar with claims in Siskiyou County at no cost.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in Dorris?
items.answer: California generally gives you two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. That timeline can be much shorter — sometimes six months — if a government entity, like a public road agency, is involved. An attorney can help pin down the exact deadline for your situation.

items.question: Does it cost anything to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free connection service, and the independent attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no upfront cost or obligation to see what your options might be.
